brief: inline dispatch: root-topic speaker coverage across 336 NPC records
outputs_expected: game/data/dialogue/topics/07-root-coverage.json (new: generic floor + cell tier + self-root actor rows)
game/src/character/converse.js — read info.cell (currently authored 39x in roots, read by NOTHING)
fix: latest rumors / latest rumours spelling split (topic-supply.js RUMOUR_TOPIC)
tools/dialogue/root-coverage.mjs (instrument, must go red when broken)
outputs_written: tools/dialogue/root-coverage.mjs — the instrument. Runs the SHIPPED reader over the SHIPPED data in bare Node; Q1 coverage, Q2 by actor, Q3 SAMENESS (the contrast guard), Q4 place. --self-test 5 pass 0 fail with four mutations.
game/data/dialogue/topics/07-root-coverage.json — 82 infos: 9 generic floor + 24 cell tier + 33 self-root actor rows + 16 earned world-root actor rows. Clears every bar in tools/check-prose.mjs.

game/src/character/converse.js — inCell(); filter field 6 read for the first time; cell scores 2 on the specificity ladder; `cell` carried on the returned info so a probe can check the choice; extras dedup against the topic list on the folded key.
game/src/engine.js — rumourFor() no longer hardcodes the second spelling; imports RUMOUR_TOPIC.
tools/quests/utility-findability.mjs — rumour regex accepts both spellings.

tools/harness/w1-speakers-ask.mjs — the browser probe (C1-C7: answers all nine in a town, the town's own answer, the contrast in the room, one gossip keyword, CONSUMPTION, delete-the-fix at the cell gate, and the conversation opened by WALKING and pressing interact). Written; awaiting a quiet box.

game/src/character/converse.js — `said_cell` on Conversation.state(): which settlement's answer the reader actually chose. infoFor() has returned `cell` since the gate was turned on and nothing could see it, so every probe had to match the town's NAME inside the prose — a test that passes whenever a line merely mentions the place.

tools/harness/w1-speakers-ask.mjs — RUN AND GREEN in two towns (14 pass / 0 fail each). C5 rebuilt town-wide and speaker-independent, C6 rebuilt on said_cell with a control and a residue scan, C7 fixed and extended to all nine roots plus a diagnostic block that says WHY a conversation did not open.
findings: start: pgrep -c headless_shell = 18, loadavg 10.59 - ABOVE the cap of 8, authoring phase first, browser verification deferred

ACTOR CENSUS, all 336 records with a `topics` array, counted off game/data/npcs/*.json: townsman 72, villager 37, legionary 31, rootkeeper 30, merchant 29, healer 29, dres-factor 25, clerk 20, innkeeper 19, mudborn 12, fisher 10, town-elder 9, sapcutter 4, outlaw 2, archivist 2, naga-elder 2, mercenary 2, deep-elder 1. EIGHTEEN names.

THE SIX ARCHETYPES (speakers.json) ARE NOT THE SAME SET AS THE ACTOR NAMES. Of the six -- rootkeeper, magister, sapcutter, archivist, mudborn, legionary -- `magister` HAS ZERO NPC RECORDS. Its province-side counterpart is the actor `dres-factor` (25 records), which answers nothing. So one of the six voices in speakers.json is written for a mouth that does not exist in the world, and the mouth that does exist has no lines. 31+30+12+4+2 = 79 answerable, which is exactly the 79 W1-26 measured.

THE UNANSWERED ARE ELEVEN NAMES, NOT TEN (the brief says ten): townsman 72, merchant 29, healer 29, dres-factor 25, innkeeper 19, fisher 10, town-elder 9, outlaw 2, naga-elder 2, mercenary 2, deep-elder 1 = 200 exactly. The 200 figure is right; the name count is 11.

NEW DEFECT, MINE, NOT PREVIOUSLY NAMED: `info.cell` IS READ BY NOTHING. infoAllowed() in converse.js checks requires/forbids/d/knows and never cell; the specificity score is (matchesActor?8)+(requires?4)+dScore+(forbids?0.5) and cell is not in it. 00-roots.json authors `cell` on 39 infos. Consequence measured below: a legionary standing in Thorn answers `specific place` with the STORMHOLD line, because among three legionary infos all scoring 8 the first authored wins. Every settlement-specific root answer in the game is currently delivered in the wrong town to everybody except the town it was written for. This is a model with no reader, RI-MTH07, one layer under the headline gap.

THE READER ALREADY HAS THE TWO-TIER SHAPE THE FIX NEEDS. converse.js infoFor(): `if (!matchesActor && info.a) continue` -- an info with `a` is locked to that actor; an info with NO `a` is usable by anyone and scores 0 against an actor-match's 8. So the generic tier exists and is EMPTY across all nine roots. The hole is not that the reader cannot express `most people say the same thing and a few say better`; it is that nobody wrote the `most people` half.

MEASURED THROUGH THE LIVE READER, BEFORE: 133 of 336 speakers could answer any root, not the 136 W1-26 reported. The three-person difference is DISPOSITION: W1-26's census did not pass one, so `d`-gated infos all opened. 1 rootkeeper and 2 mudborn sit below their own archetype's `d` bar. Pass the speaker's real base disposition and the honest before-figure is 133.

THE CELL DEFECT, CONFIRMED AND FIXED. 267 of the 1,065 infos in game/data/dialogue/topics/** carry `cell` and NOTHING read it. Turning the gate on moved `specific-place` from 133 answerable to 88 (people who only ever had another town's line now correctly get none) and its DISTINCT answers from 7 to 9 — all nine settlement lines became reachable in their own town, where before only three could ever fire whatever town you stood in. BLAST RADIUS across every non-root topic: own-topic offers 332 -> 329, records offering zero topics 155 -> 155. Three lines lost, seven towns' worth of wrong answers removed.
AFTER: coverage 133 -> 336 of 336. All EIGHTEEN actor names answer all nine roots (mean 9.00 each). DULLNESS 28.9% against a 60% ceiling. 736 cell-gated answers delivered, 0 misplaced.

THE INSTRUMENT WENT RED FIRST AND FOR THE RIGHT REASONS. Before the fix --self-test was 2 pass / 3 fail: M1 (strip the generic tier) could not move coverage BECAUSE THERE WAS NO GENERIC TIER, and M4 declared its own place check VACUOUS rather than passing on zero cell-gated deliveries. Both now pass.

MY OWN M3 MUTATION WAS BROKEN AND LOOKED LIKE A BROKEN METRIC. It filtered topics on `t.root`, but only the DECLARING file carries that flag — buildTopicIndex ORs it onto the merged record so 06-opening-roots and 07-root-coverage add root infos without re-declaring it. So the mutation missed the villager and clerk halves entirely and plateaued at 51.9% instead of 100%. Take the root roster off the INDEX, never off a file.

THE SPELLING SPLIT HAD EXACTLY THREE SITES: topic-supply.js RUMOUR_TOPIC, engine.js rumourFor() (which hardcoded the string rather than using the constant), and a regex in tools/quests/utility-findability.mjs. Every authored data file already used the root spelling.

AND FOLDING THE SPELLING EXPOSED A SECOND BUG IT HAD BEEN HIDING: Conversation.start() pushes every `extra` onto the list with no dedup. While the two spellings were distinct that produced two keywords for one subject; once folded it would have produced the SAME keyword twice in one list. Extras now REPLACE a matching list entry, which is also the right precedence — say() resolves extras first, so what the town is actually saying beats the province-wide 'ask at the inn'.

PROSE: the file failed tools/check-prose.mjs on first draft — sting 42.19 (ceiling 6.0), contractions 661 (band top 365), 9 `-body` forms, zero conjunction openers. SIX stings, all of the same shape: a closing 'That's the ...' recast. Flattened by hand, and the contraction overshoot cut by un-contracting the FORMAL voices only (dres-factor, naga-elder, deep-elder, town-elder, healer) rather than sweeping the file — which buys voice differentiation instead of a uniform offset. Final: sting 0.00, questions 81.7 (floor 39.8), exclamations 20.4 (band 5.3-42.6), contractions 190.6, fragopen 0.00. The file appears in no warning.
155 of 336 records are offered ZERO of their OWN topics (before and after my change alike). Not mine and not caused by me — banked so it is not rediscovered.

THE MIRROR OF THE HEADLINE DEFECT, FOUND AND MEASURED, NOT FIXED (owner call, named so it is not rediscovered): 40 infos in game/data/dialogue/topics/** are written for an actor name that NO NPC RECORD IN THE BUILD WEARS. magister 23, notary 6, dockhand 3, walker 3, scribe 2, vakh-speaker 1, smuggler 1, harbourmistress 1. Same root cause as the headline — nothing ever joined the roster in game/data/npcs/** to the `a` fields in the dialogue — and just as invisible, because a dead info does not error, it simply never gets scored. `magister` is one of the SIX archetypes in speakers.json: a whole voice slot, with calibrated fingerprint targets and its own address form ('provincial'), written for a mouth that does not exist. Its world-side counterpart is `dres-factor` (25 records). Whether the fix is to rename the actor on 25 NPC records or to alias the two in the reader is a DATA-OWNERSHIP decision, not a coverage one, so I measured it (root-coverage.mjs Q5) and left it. I did NOT silently alias another piece's voice slot.

IN PLAY, `latest rumors` IS NOT THE 65%-dull line the census reports. 321 of 336 speakers have a live settlement rumour from dialogue/rumours.json, and after the extras-dedup fix that rumour REPLACES the generic root entry. The census tool measures infoFor() alone and cannot see the supply, so 65% is its ceiling, not the played figure. Stated so nobody quotes the wrong one.
AFTER adding a `someone-in-particular` place tier: overall DULLNESS 28.9% -> 25.2%, that root's commonest line 51% -> 18%, cell-gated deliveries 736 -> 848, still 0 misplaced.

game/data/index.json regenerates via tools/analysis/data-index.mjs; it had already picked up the new file, and --check is clean. A dialogue file not in the index does not load in the browser, so this is worth confirming before any browser pass.

SUCCESSOR RE-RUN at commit 0b2d6ef (clean tree; orchestrator banked the predecessor's work): instrument still GREEN. coverage 336/336 all nine roots, dullness 25.2%, misplaced 0 of 848 cell-gated, 40 dead-actor infos reported. --self-test now 9 pass 0 fail (predecessor's file said 5; three M5 spelling/gossip assertions and an M1 full-coverage split have been added). Numbers survived the two commits that landed after they were taken.

BROWSER RUN 1 (commit 0b2d6ef, 6 browsers / loadavg 2.4): 8 pass 2 fail. BOTH FAILURES WERE THE PROBE, NOT THE WORLD, and the node census was right. C1-C5 passed on the first browser run: a merchant in Gideon who could answer NOTHING before this round answers all nine out loud; two trades in one town differ 3/3 on the self-roots and agree 2/3 on the world-roots; ONE gossip keyword; and the CONSUMPTION mutation silenced the person and restoring it gave back the identical words.

C6's FAILURE WAS A CHECK DEMANDING THAT A CORRECT ANSWER BE WRONG. It watched `services` and asserted the line must change when the speaker moves town. For a MERCHANT, `services` resolves to the `a: merchant` actor row (specificity 8) which beats the cell tier (2) — a line about the trade, not the town, and right to follow them to Thorn. The 0-misplaced figure from the node census was never in question. Rewritten to split the nine by what the reader ACTUALLY CHOSE and to carry a control: cell-gated answers must change, cell-less answers must not.

AND C6 COULD NOT HAVE BEEN WRITTEN CORRECTLY, because `Conversation.state()` reported `greeting_cell` but never `said_cell` — infoFor() has returned `cell` since the gate was turned on and NOTHING could see it. Any probe asking 'did they give me GIDEON's line?' had to match the town's name inside the prose, which passes whenever a line merely mentions the place. Added `said_cell` to state() (one line, mirrors greeting_cell, no behaviour change).

C7's FAILURE WAS THREE WRONG API FACTS IN FOUR LINES: an NPC's `pos` is the ARRAY [x,y,z] not {x,z} (so the teleport went to NaN); queueInputs events are {f, press, release} with `f` an OFFSET from the current frame, and {frame, down, up} is REFUSED by the fail-closed key check; and interact only sets `_talkPending` — talkTo runs in _afterStep, so too few frames after the press looks exactly like a reach failure. C7 now also asks all nine rather than one, and asserts the button reached the PERSON and not a prop standing near them.

BROWSER RUN 2: C7 GREEN — the conversation opened by TELEPORTING BESIDE THE PERSON AND PRESSING INTERACT reached fence-ashul at 1.08 m, offered 11 topics, and answered all nine IDENTICALLY to the eid-named conversation (9/9). The coverage numbers are about the surface a player touches.

AND C6 FAILED AGAIN FOR A THIRD, REAL REASON, which the new said_cell field made legible in one line: after setting settlement='thorn' the answers still came back cell=gideon. inCell() reads FIVE fields (settlement, cell, interior, home_interior, work_interior) and matches a PREFIX, so `interior: "gideon-lowmarket"` satisfies cell:"gideon" by itself. Moving one field left the speaker in Gideon by four other names, and the town answer was RIGHT not to move. A partial perturbation is indistinguishable from a dead gate.

THE SETTLEMENT RUMOUR IS A SECOND PLACE CHANNEL AND IT BROKE MY OWN CONTROL HONESTLY. `latest-rumors` carries no `cell` yet changed when the body moved: Engine._installTopicSupply hands the speaker their settlement's live rumour as an EXTRA which replaces the root's generic answer. So place-sensitivity has two independent mechanisms and only one of them is the cell gate. Counting it as a control break charged the world for correct behaviour; it now has its own assertion (and it is the observable half of the spelling fix — the supply only reaches the root because the two spellings fold to one key).

MY OWN 'DERIVE THE MUTATION FROM THE DATA' FIX WAS TOO BROAD AND ONLY THE SECOND TOWN CAUGHT IT. Rewriting every string on the record that named the old town also rewrote the ID: Stormhold's records are named `stormhold-apothecary-1`, so the eid changed under the probe and the next talkTo threw `nobody by that name is in the world`. Gideon survived it only because `fence-ashul` does not begin with its town's name. A perturbation must move ONE property; that one moved identity as well as place. RUNNING THE SAME PROBE IN A SECOND TOWN IS WHAT FOUND IT — one town is not a control.

TOPIC IDS VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY (brief item 2): all nine ids in 07-root-coverage.json are declared as `root` elsewhere in game/data/dialogue/topics/ (so the file EXTENDS the roster rather than re-declaring it), and it makes ZERO unresolvable `to:` references against the 453 topic ids declared corpus-wide.

TIDEWRACK IS NOT A COVERAGE GAP AND SHOULD NOT BE 'FIXED'. The settlement census is helstrom 58, lilmoth 50, stormhold 49, gideon 41, blackrose 34, archon 34, soulrest 29, thorn 23, tidewrack 3, and 15 with NO settlement. tidewrack has no cell row on any world root while all eight province towns do — because its three records ARE THE OPENING (jeeh-ei, warden-scribe-tuleeh-ma, clerk-avelia-doren, actors villager and clerk), already served by 06-opening-roots.json. The 15 with no settlement correctly get the generic floor: they are not standing in a town.

THE SHAPE, AS BUILT AND MEASURED: generic floor 1 per root (9); self-roots duties/my-trade/background carry 11 actor rows each and NO cell rows; the place roots specific-place/services/little-advice carry 8 town rows each and someone-in-particular 5; and 15 earned world-root actor rows across five roots. someone-in-particular deliberately covers only 5 of 8 towns — the other three fall to the province-wide floor, which is the Morrowind shape working, not a hole to fill.

check-data / check-quests / check-content all exit 0; boot-check PASSES and lives at tools/harness/boot-check.mjs, NOT tools/boot-check.mjs (running the latter gives MODULE_NOT_FOUND with exit code 0 through a pipe, which reads as a pass — worth knowing).

PROSE, re-measured on the shipped file: 07-root-coverage.json sting 0.00 (reference 3.42), questions 75.52 per 10k against a corpus dialogue average of 36.40 — the file pulls the register toward the reference rather than away — exclamations 18.88 (reference 21.30), fragopen 0.00, contractions 176.21. check-prose reports 3 registers inside the ratchet and names my file in no warning.

C7's SECOND FAILURE WAS THE WORLD BEING RIGHT AGAIN, and the one-line diagnostic block I added is what said so: visible=false, npc_interior=stormhold-house-1, world_interior=null, y_gap=1.40 m. Stormhold's first previously-mute actor is an apothecary standing INSIDE A HOUSE while the player is on the street — 1 m away in plan, 1.4 m below, correctly unreachable. 'no conversation' is the single symptom of four different causes (out of reach / not present / a prop or signpost took the button / a different interior) and guessing between them costs a browser run each time.

AND THE FIX FOR IT EXPOSED A THIRD: `n.visible` IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE RECORD. sim/npc.js derives it from `n.at` against `sim.env.interior` and only writes it when it CHANGES, so straight after loadState every NPC still carries the spec default `true` and 'can I reach this person' answers yes for everybody. Two frames of stepping before the roster is read fixes it and uses the SHIPPED presence rule instead of a second copy that can drift.

C5 FAILED IN THE SECOND TOWN FOR A REASON THAT WOULD HAVE AIMED THE NEXT WRITER BACKWARDS. It stripped the floor from ONE root and watched ONE speaker; `little-secret` carries an `a: townsman` row, so Stormhold's townsman answers from their own line and removing the floor could not silence them. That is the coverage design WORKING — most fall to the floor, a few have better — and the check called it an orphan model. A check that reads the contrast as a defect punishes the exact thing the round exists to protect.

C5 IS NOW SPEAKER-INDEPENDENT AND THE NUMBERS ARE BETTER EVIDENCE: strip every info with neither an actor nor a cell (the true floor, nothing else) and count (person, root) pairs across the whole town. Gideon 369 -> 351 -> 369 (18 answers lost and all 18 restored) across 41 people; Stormhold 441 -> 424 -> 441 across 49. One speaker can be lucky; forty cannot. That the loss is 4-5% and not 50% is the design: the floor is the last resort, under the cell tier and the actor rows.

FINAL BROWSER RESULT, BOTH TOWNS, at commit e0863b7 with 18-26 headless_shell and loadavg 14-17 (ABOVE the cap of 8 — every figure here is a count or a boolean, which survive contention; no timing is reported): town-gideon 14 pass 0 fail, town-stormhold 14 pass 0 fail. A merchant in Gideon and a street sweeper in Stormhold, both wearing actor names that answered NOTHING before this round, were WALKED TO and asked all nine words with the interact button, and answered all nine identically to the eid-named conversation.

RUNNING THE SAME PROBE IN A SECOND TOWN FOUND FOUR SEPARATE DEFECTS THAT GIDEON PASSED THROUGH: the over-broad relocation that renamed the NPC (ids are `stormhold-apothecary-1`, `fence-ashul` is not), the indoors speaker C7 could not reach, the stale `visible` flag, and the one-speaker consumption check. ONE TOWN IS NOT A CONTROL — this is the same lesson as 'vary when you save, not just what'.

THE TREE MOVED UNDER ME AND IT VINDICATED THE SHAPE DECISION IN THE STRONGEST POSSIBLE WAY. Re-measuring at commit e0863b7 the census is no longer 336 records but 347: another agent added ELEVEN NPCs wearing eleven BRAND-NEW ACTOR NAMES (agaceph-guide, agaceph-weir, paatru-clay, paatru-edge, sarpa-flier, archein-holder, archein-factor, sap-speaker, miredancer-elder, deadwater-warrior, antiquarian). Coverage is 347 of 347, all nine roots, mean 9.00 each — and NOT ONE LINE WAS WRITTEN FOR ANY OF THEM. Dullness 25.2% -> 25.4%, misplaced still 0 of 890.

THAT IS THE ARGUMENT FOR THE SHAPE, SETTLED BY EVENT RATHER THAN BY REASONING. Had the round been built as 'an answer per actor' — 11 actors x 9 roots — these eleven new names would have re-opened the EXACT defect it closed, eleven more mute actors, within hours of the fix landing. Because the fix is a generic FLOOR with an actor tier above it rather than a table keyed on actor, a name nobody has ever heard of arrives already able to answer the nine words, and the province stays legible while it grows. A per-actor table would have needed an edit per new name forever.

THE ELEVEN NEW NAMES CURRENTLY ANSWER THE THREE SELF-ROOTS (duties, my-trade, background) FROM THE GENERIC FLOOR. That is correct and not a gap — it is precisely 'most people give the same generic reply' — but it is where a successor with prose budget should spend it: a sap-speaker and a deadwater-warrior saying the same thing about their own trade is the one place the floor is doing work the contrast would rather it did not.

FINAL STATE, re-measured at e0863b7 immediately before finishing: root-coverage GREEN 347/347, dullness 25.4%, misplaced 0/890, --self-test 9 pass 0 fail. check-data, check-quests, check-content and tools/harness/boot-check.mjs all exit 0. check-prose names 07-root-coverage.json in no warning. Browser probe 14 pass / 0 fail in each of two towns.

NO SCREENSHOT BANKED, DELIBERATELY: at finish the box was at 24 headless_shell / loadavg 18.8, far above the cap of 8, and a capture taken there is both expensive and distorted. The blog line (mandatory) is written; the interesting artefact of this piece is a transcript rather than a picture, and reports/journeys/w1-speakers-ask*.json carries the full nine answers from both speakers for a writer to quote directly.
notes_for_successor:
W1-SPEAKERS IS DONE AND VERIFIED IN THE RUNNING WORLD. Both probes are green; re-run `node tools/dialogue/root-coverage.mjs` and `node tools/harness/w1-speakers-ask.mjs --state town-gideon|town-stormhold` to check nothing has rotted.
THE ONE PIECE OF WORK I AM DELIBERATELY LEAVING: eleven new actor names (agaceph-*, paatru-*, sarpa-flier, archein-*, sap-speaker, miredancer-elder, deadwater-warrior, antiquarian) landed mid-run and answer the three SELF-roots from the generic floor. They are covered and the world is consistent; what they lack is a voice of their own on duties/my-trade/background. That is a prose job with a clear bar (tools/check-prose.mjs, and W1-PROSE-R2's earned-sting rule) and a clear ceiling: root-coverage.mjs Q3 DULLNESS must go DOWN and must never be closed by giving everybody a bespoke line.
NOT MINE AND STILL OPEN, measured and banked above: 40 infos written for an actor no NPC record wears (magister 23 of them, and magister is one of the SIX archetypes in speakers.json with its own calibrated fingerprint — its world-side counterpart is `dres-factor`, 25 records). Renaming 25 records vs aliasing the two in the reader is a data-ownership decision, not a coverage one. root-coverage.mjs Q5 reports it every run.
ALSO STILL OPEN: 155 of 336 records are offered ZERO of their OWN topics (unchanged by this round, not caused by it).
THE METHOD LESSON WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX: run the probe in a SECOND TOWN. Gideon passed through four separate probe defects that Stormhold caught — an over-broad relocation that renamed the NPC, a speaker standing indoors that interact correctly could not reach, a `visible` flag that is not computed until the sim steps, and a one-speaker consumption check that a lucky actor row could satisfy. Every one of them would have shipped as a green run.
